title: build(spec): one module graph with shared chunks, so each schema ships once and is one object across entries
body:
Fixes #8133

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: none

## What changes

`@objectstack/spec`'s JS build is now **one esbuild module graph with shared chunks** for every output (ESM and CJS, Node and `browser`-conditioned). A module two entries reach is one module in one `dist/chunk-HASH.{mjs,js}` file, so it ships once and is the same object through either entry. Only `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` changes behaviour. The `exports` map and the declaration build are untouched.

### Why a bare `splitting: true` was not enough (measured, then rejected)

With `splitting: true` on the existing two passes, `./shared` and `./migrations` (subpaths with no `browser` condition, so a browser bundler loads their ordinary bundles) started linking the chunk that imports `pg-connection-string`. esbuild assigns a module to a chunk by **file-level** reachability, so an entry links every chunk its import graph touches, used or not. Per-entry tree-shaking had kept them clean. That is the breakage class `check:browser-reachable-entries` rule 2 refuses: the controlled experiment below failed to bundle with `Could not resolve "fs"`. A plain two-pass split would also have left the browser graph and the Node graph as two copies of everything they share.

### What the config does instead (`oneModuleGraph`)

- **One graph.** Entries: the 19 ordinary outputs at `dist/ENTRY` plus the 5 `browser`-conditioned outputs at `dist/browser/ENTRY`. The browser swap of the pg-grammar arm (the 2026-08-22 ruling's mechanism, keyed to the same seam specifier) now applies to the whole graph.
- **Node-side copy of only the seam's importers.** The Node outputs of the 5 `browser`-conditioned entries are built from a `node-side` esbuild namespace. It re-instantiates exactly the modules from which the seam is reachable (measured at BASE: **28 of 459** source modules: the entry barrels, the driver configs, the datasource, stack and conversion/migration registries). Every other module resolves back to the shared graph.
- **Measured per build, not listed.** A metafile pre-pass over those entries' Node graph computes the set. It **refuses the build** when no module imports the seam any more: then the `browser` conditions are moot, and withdrawing them is a decision.
- **Behaviour unchanged.** The Node outputs of the conditioned entries still run the pg grammar. Every other output still never runs it. Their per-entry bundles linked no pg grammar at all, which the gate held at BASE. Where a chunk they share reaches the driver configs, they now carry the browser twin.

## Measurements

All readings are on this worktree. BASE = `origin/main` `47af3dd`. HEAD = `5a40a420` (this branch with `origin/main` `c61f75d1` merged; every HEAD reading below was re-taken there, and was identical at the pre-merge head `19a8800a` except the experiment, 602.9 KB there). Full `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` both times.

| | BASE | HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| `a.defineConnector === b.defineConnector` (root vs `/integration`), ESM | false | **true** |
| same, CJS | false | **true** |
| shared object/function exports identical across entries, `browser` view (119 pairs) | 0 | **119** |
| same, Node view (119 pairs) | 0 | **114** |
| `.mjs` files defining `var FieldSchema =` | 14 | **1** |
| `.mjs` files defining `var ConnectorSchema =` | 3 | **1** |
| total `packages/spec/dist` | 123.5M | **53.5M** |
| JS + maps (excl. `.d.ts`) | 93.9M | **23.9M** |
| declaration files | 134 | 134 (same set, hash-stripped) |
| objectui import experiment, gzip 9 | 1,628.4 KB | **603.6 KB** (−63%) |

- **Node view, 5 not identical.** All 5 are root vs `/shared`: `MAP_SUPPORTED_FIELDS`, `METADATA_ALIASES`, `normalizeMetadataCollection`, `normalizePluginMetadata`, `normalizeStackInput`. They live in `shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts`, which reaches the seam, so the root's Node output carries the node-side copy and `/shared` (unconditioned) the shared one. Under the `browser` condition they are one object.
- **`ConnectorSchema` on the card.** The card's `a.ConnectorSchema === b.ConnectorSchema` compares `undefined` to an object: the root entry does not export `ConnectorSchema` at top level, before or after. Only `/integration` does. `defineConnector` is the meaningful half, and it holds.
- **Controlled experiment.** The card's experiment, re-derived on today's trees. objectui `a3c0da9` (current `main`) value imports: **256 symbols across 11 subpaths**, parsed with the TypeScript parser, type-only imports excluded. Each import comes from the subpath objectui uses. esbuild `bundle` + `minify` + `platform: browser`, gzip level 9, zod bundled in every arm.
  - BASE per-entry `dist`: **1,628.4 KB**.
  - HEAD `dist`: **603.6 KB**.
  - Control, one module graph from `src` with the same pure-annotation and swap plugins: **538.5 KB**.
  - The card's figures (1,542 / 452 KB on `18.0.0`, 232 symbols) are the same shape on an older tree.
- **Chunk graph.** Acyclic in both formats: 0 cycles over 1,181 ESM and 1,158 CJS relative edges. This is why CJS takes shared chunks safely (Rollup converts each chunk ESM→CJS under tsup's `treeshake`, with no partially-initialized `require`). `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` loads every `require` entry and is green.

**NOT MEASURED: objectui `Bundle Analysis` `vendor-objectstack`.** That number comes from objectui CI on a pin that carries this change: objectui's own pin move, which also re-baselines its eager-closure ceilings. The experiment above is the local stand-in, not that number.

## Deep-path consumers (risk: chunk names are not stable)

- **objectui** `a3c0da9`: three `@objectstack/spec/dist/index.{js,mjs}` strings, all regex probe inputs in tests, not imports (`scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts:481`, `:946`, `:1165`; `scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-client-dist.test.ts:398`). Both files still exist.
  - `scripts/objectstack-pin.mjs` hard-links the package's whole tree, so chunks travel with it.
  - The `vendor-objectstack` group test matches any file under the package directory, so chunks group there.
- **HotCRM** `a4b3560`: zero `@objectstack/spec/dist` / `src` / `json-schema` deep imports.

## Gates and tests

All on `5a40a420` unless stated. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.

- **Derived union** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`): 72 commands. **71 exit 0, 1 exit 1** (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:liveness`, the main-red below). `--ran` reconciliation: `72 derived, 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, a derived zero from 72 recorded exit codes. On the pre-merge head `19a8800a`, all 72 exited 0. One of them, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, first exited 3 because of a shallow clone, then 0 after `git fetch --depth=1` of its pinned fixture commit.
- **Dist-reading gates on `5a40a420`:** `check:browser-reachable-entries` (48 bundles walked transitively; 10 server-only links, all on the Node side of the 5 conditioned entries), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:published-files` and `check:dev-prereqs` (local-only; after rebuilding the two packages the merge moved): all exit 0.
- **Whole workspace build** at `19a8800a`, `pnpm build`: `Tasks: 76 successful, 76 total`, `examples/*` included.
- **Every consumer's tests** at `19a8800a`, root `pnpm test` (`turbo run test test:repo`, all 152 tasks, every package that reads `@objectstack/spec` through `dist`): `Tasks: 152 successful, 152 total`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The run was interrupted once by a worker restart and resumed from turbo's cache: 125 cached, 27 executed in the second run, and no failure in either run.
  - Inside it, the dogfood battery: Test Files 295 passed, 3 skipped (298); Tests 2520 passed, 18 skipped (2538).
  - `@objectstack/cli` (unit + integration): 500 passed, 1 skipped (501); Tests 6291 passed.
  - `packages/qa/downstream-contract`: 3 files / 31 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/spec`: `test` 721/721 files, `test:repo` 79/79.
- **`@objectstack/spec` on `5a40a420`:** `typecheck` exit 0, including the test layer that compiles `tsup.config.ts` through `pure-schema-construction.test.ts` (that reading was taken at `19a8800a`). `test` gives 720 passed, 1 failed (721); the failing file is `scripts/liveness/check-liveness.test.ts` (23 tests), the same main-red. `test:repo` was not reached after it.
- **Declaration build unaffected:** the DTS-pass options object (`BUILD_DTS=true`, plugins by name) is identical at BASE and HEAD (sha256 prefix `ccf850853f3c0699`). There are 134 declaration files, the same set once hashes are stripped. The DTS pass is not byte-stable from run to run (`tsup.config.ts`'s docblock), so it is compared by its inputs and its file set, not by a digest.
- **Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each leg verified on disk, each restored blob-identical to `HEAD` `9c9b83dc`, then rebuilt). Predicted, then observed:
  - **A1** (browser swap off): predicted red on rule 2. Observed red, 14 problems: all 10 `dist/browser/**` bundles plus `./shared` and `./migrations` in both formats. The first attempt was refused by the tool as a no-op (the replacement was a substring of the anchor), so nothing ran; re-run with a unique replacement.
  - **A2** (node-side twinning off): predicted a positive-control red. Observed `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED`.
  - **A3** (seam regex matches nothing): predicted the build refuses. Observed `one-module-graph: no module of the Node graph of … imports the pg-grammar arm` in both the ESM and CJS runs.
  - Restore leg: rebuilt, `check:browser-reachable-entries` green, every measurement identical.

**Main-red, not this PR's: `check:liveness` and `check-liveness.test.ts`.** Green on `19a8800a`, red after merging `origin/main` `c61f75d1`, and still red on `origin/main` `f9a1e93f`. This PR's diff vs `main` touches no ledger, no `service-automation` file and nothing under `src/`.
- **The failing row.** The ledger row `translation/flows.screens` cites `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts#renderFlowTextSlot`.
- **Why it was green before.** `engine.ts` named `screens` only through a comment ("two screens down"). `0189524a` (#25734) moved that comment into `run-resume.ts`.
- **Why a repoint is not enough.** `renderFlowTextSlot` itself now lives in `node-text-rendering.ts`, which never names `screens` either.
- **Proposed patch, for the owning lane (not applied here).** Drop the `engine.ts#renderFlowTextSlot` clause from that row's `evidence`. `builtin/screen-nodes.ts#registerScreenNodes`, already cited, is the reader that spells the key. Or cite `node-text-rendering.ts#renderFlowTextSlot` with an evidence-scope note. Fix PR known to this run: none.

CI on this PR is the authority for the families above: the required five, Build Core's bundle-size step, Test Core.

## Acceptance notes

- **Comments under `packages/spec/src/**` that describe the old layout.** The dispatch puts `src/**` out of scope, so they are not edited here. Each is now inaccurate about the layout, not about behaviour:
  - `src/index.ts:73`: "Every subpath entry is a self-contained bundle".
  - `src/conversions/registry.ts:18144`: "Each published entry is one flat file (`tsup.config.ts`, `splitting: false`)". The PURE-annotation reasoning it supports still holds per chunk.
  - `src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts:40`: a historical sentence. Its TSDoc renders into the generated `content/docs/references/api/package-api-assembled.mdx`.

  Proposed: one comment-only follow-up, routed by the seat.
- `packages/spec/README.md` (published) is corrected here. `check:browser-reachable-entries`' docblock said "this tree cannot exercise" a chunk walk; now it does, and the docblock says so.
